subject: Request: authorize rollforward to model-8x-slim for Textopia — P95 mitigation
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: authorize rollforward to model-8x-slim for Textopia — P95 mitigation

Team,

We started seeing a sustained P95 latency increase for Textopia (prod, model-8x v2.3) at ~07:40 PDT (see attached short report). Over the last 90 minutes p95 has moved from ~260ms to ~520ms for their main chat route, and SLA alerts triggered. Traffic pattern hasn't changed on their side (they confirmed request size/distribution), and preliminary traces point to longer attention windows and increased KV cache churn on the current compiled kernel on A100s.

Engineering (Vivek) and SRE (Jonas) ran a quick triage and propose a rollforward to model-8x-slim (v2.3-slim), our quantized/optimized variant that reduces per-token compute and keeps functional parity for Textopia's prompt patterns. This is a rollforward (deploy faster variant) rather than a rollback, which should avoid user-facing output regressions we've seen with older checkpoints. Expected impact: drop P95 to ~280–320ms during canary; cost delta minimal (+2–3%).

Requesting:
- Approval to perform a canary rollforward to model-8x-slim on Textopia's prod route at the 12:00–12:30 PDT maintenance window (canary 5% traffic for 30m -> 25% for 30m -> 100% if green).
- Temporary SLA exception for p95 breach for up to 48 hours during the mitigation window and measurement period (we will revert if quality metrics degrade).

Attachments: p95_latency_breakdown_20270411.pdf (short dashboard snapshot), model8x_kvcache_dumps.zip (traces/snippets).

Notes:
- Fallback: automatic revert to v2.2 if generation quality or error rates increase beyond guardrails.
- Communication: I propose notifying Textopia's engineering lead (Sam) and CS (Marissa) now and sending customer-facing note if we go to 25%+ traffic.

Irene
Irene Choi
Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference


---

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: authorize rollforward to model-8x-slim for Textopia — P95 mitigation

Irene — thanks for the summary. Quick clarifications from infra side:
- Root cause hypothesis: increased average prompt length + a handful of long-running KV cache misses due to recently enabled session affinity for Textopia (they rolled sticky sessions last week). That combination pushes attention compute into worst-case kernels.
- Model-8x-slim is compiled with a better fused attention kernel and lower-precision matmuls; we've validated parity on our eval set for Textopia's top-50 prompts.
- Canary plan looks good. We need a signed "operational go" (explicit approve) because this touches their prod routing and we will run a short no-op fallback exercise beforehand.

Operational asks:
1) Approve explicit canary start window: 2027-04-11 19:00 UTC (12:00 PDT).
2) Approve 48-hour SLA exception window. We will record metrics to the console and tag this run SERV-8421.
3) Confirm customer notification cadence (Irene/Marissa to send).

If we get approvals I will kick the rollforward with Jonas coordinating the canary and console dashboards.

-Vivek
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700

Thanks for the heads up, Irene and team. We noticed some slowness on our side starting ~07:45 PDT; it caused a small spike in user complaints but nothing production-critical yet. Our engineering lead confirms we didn't change client-side batching or prompt templates this morning.

We're 👍 on a canary that reduces latency quickly — prefer rollforward over rollback if it preserves output quality. Please share any customer-facing note you plan to send before 12:00 PDT so we can align.

-Sam
VP of Product
Textopia Inc.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Approve: rollforward to model-8x-slim + temporary SLA exception (Textopia)

Approved. Per discussion with Product and CS, we will: 
- Authorize the canary rollforward at 2027-04-11 19:00 UTC (12:00 PDT).
- Grant a 48-hour temporary SLA exception for P95 breaches tied to this mitigation (conditioned on active monitoring and automatic rollback guardrails).
- Require a customer-facing note to be sent to Textopia 30 minutes before we move to 25% traffic; Irene please coordinate copy with Sam.

Jonas/Vivek: run the canary, watch error rates and quality guardrails closely. If quality regression > 0.6% (top-5 prompts) or error-rate > 0.2% absolute, revert immediately and notify Laura and Marissa.

I'll log the approval in SERV-8421 and message Sales/GTM.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
